title: My Grandmother's Hands: Racialized Trauma and the Mending of Our Bodies and Hearts
author: Resmaa Menakem
target_audience: Individuals interested in understanding racism and trauma
Therapists, counselors, and other mental health professionals
People seeking tools for healing personal or generational trauma
Readers invested in anti-racism work and social justice
core_themes: Healing practices for individuals and communities
The impact of white supremacy on all bodies
The connections among personal, communal, and systemic healing
primary_purpose: To explore how racialized trauma lives in the bodies of Black, White, and police Americans, offering readers psychological, somatic, and communal tools for recognizing, understanding, and healing this trauma, thereby fostering real change and collective well-being.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, compassionate, and direct, with stories, science, and practical exercises
structure_format.organization: Divided into sections addressing Black bodies, White bodies, and police bodies, with chapters featuring personal stories, conceptual reflections, and guided body practices

key_concepts_lessons: Trauma is experienced and held in the body, not just the mind.
Racism in America is not only a sociopolitical problem, but also a deeply rooted physiological one that affects everyone.
Healing racialized trauma requires body-centered approaches, including mindfulness, breathing, and movement exercises.
Both Black and White Americans—and law enforcement personnel—carry inherited trauma in distinct ways.
Addressing racialized trauma necessitates individual, communal, and systemic change.
Compassion, self-awareness, and community support are critical in the process of healing generational wounds.
notable_features: Integration of science, storytelling, and somatic (body-focused) exercises
Focus on embodiment and bodily awareness as a means to heal trauma
Direct address to readers of various racial backgrounds, including specific sections for Black, White, and police readers
Widely utilized in anti-racism, diversity, and trauma-informed trainings
cultural_historical_context: Published amid ongoing national conversations about race, policing, and trauma in the United States, the book draws on contemporary neuroscience, psychology, and bodywork traditions. It speaks to a renewed societal focus on both understanding generational trauma and advancing meaningful racial healing.
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed for its accessible, innovative approach to trauma and racial healing
Adopted by therapists, activists, and educators as a core resource in anti-racism and trauma-informed practices
Praise for its practical exercises and compassionate, nuanced framing of a complex subject
Catalyzed conversations about the need for somatic (body-based) approaches in addressing systemic racism
comparable_titles: The Body Keeps the Score by Bessel van der Kolk
Stamped from the Beginning by Ibram X. Kendi
Between the World and Me by Ta-Nehisi Coates
Trauma and Recovery by Judith Herman
Heal Your Body by Louise Hay (for mind-body connection themes)
